reasoning: The core problem — that fine-tuning (including on purely benign data) erodes LLM safety alignment — is the well-established finding of Qi et al. 2023 (arXiv:2310.03693), and the LoRA/PEFT-specific version is documented by Lermen et al. (arXiv:2310.20624, "LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training") plus a large body of follow-on work (SafeLoRA, SaLoRA, etc.). Both of the proposal's claimed twists over Qi et al. are already covered: (1) PEFT/LoRA rather than full FT is the explicit subject of multiple papers showing LoRA erodes safety, with some finding LoRA poses a greater safety risk than full FT under identical data; and (2) rank-as-an-explicit-knob is directly studied, with published results reporting misalignment increasing monotonically with LoRA rank (e.g., 39.12 at r=8 to 71.38 at r=256) and that "all ranks of LoRA degrade much more rapidly than full fine-tuning, with low ranks degrading the most." The proposed experiment (baseline refusal rate, LoRA/QLoRA on benign instruction data, rank sweep r=4/8/16/32, re-measure refusal with a judge) would essentially replicate existing published results rather than fill an open gap.

evidence.title: Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To! (Qi et al.)
evidence.summary: Foundational paper establishing that fine-tuning aligned LLMs erodes safety, including with benign/utility-oriented datasets; even ~100 benign samples can degrade safety. This is the work the proposal explicitly positions itself against.

evidence.title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training in Llama 2-Chat (Lermen et al.)
evidence.summary: Directly demonstrates the PEFT twist: LoRA (and QLoRA) fine-tuning efficiently and significantly reduces refusal rates of Llama 2-Chat 7B/13B/70B, undoing safety training cheaply on a single consumer GPU.

evidence.title: SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation
evidence.summary: States that safety alignment deteriorates when users fine-tune with LoRA even when all fine-tuning samples are benign, and that LoRA fine-tuning can pose a greater safety risk than full fine-tuning under identical data; motivates rank/subspace analysis.

evidence.title: SC-LoRA / related benign-data + rank studies
evidence.summary: Search surfaced quantitative findings that misalignment increases monotonically with LoRA rank (misalignment score ~39.12 at rank 8 rising to ~71.38 at rank 256), directly addressing the proposal's 'rank as an explicit knob' contribution.

evidence.title: LoRA Fine-tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training
evidence.summary: Community write-up of the LoRA-undoes-safety result, confirming the PEFT-erodes-safety problem is widely known and reproduced in the safety community.

evidence.title: What is in Your Safe Data? Identifying Benign Data that Breaks Safety
evidence.summary: Studies precisely which benign data breaks safety alignment during fine-tuning, confirming the benign-data-erodes-safety problem is solved and analyzed at a fine-grained level.
